extracted.intended_audience: drug applicants and nonapplicants (manufacturers, packers, distributors) responsible for FDA postmarketing reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and content standards for submitting postmarketing adverse drug experience reports, periodic and other postmarketing reports, recordkeeping, electronic submission format, and waivers to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

rubrics_metrics.name: General reporting obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit to FDA adverse drug experience information as described in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in paragraph (g)(2) of this section, these reports must be submitted to the Agency in electronic format as described in paragraph (g)(1) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing 15-day "Alert reports" (initial timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must report each adverse drug experience that is both serious and unexpected, whether foreign or domestic, as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days from initial receipt of the information by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to both foreign and domestic reports that are serious and unexpected; timing is measured from initial receipt by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing 15-day "Alert reports" followup
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must promptly investigate all adverse drug experiences that are the subject of these postmarketing 15-day Alert reports and must submit followup reports within 15 calendar days of receipt of new information or as requested by FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional information is not obtainable, records should be maintained of the unsuccessful steps taken to seek additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonapplicant submission option and recordkeeping (5-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonapplicants (persons other than the applicant whose name appears on the label as manufacturer, packer, or distributor) may meet obligations by submitting all reports of serious adverse drug experiences to the applicant. If a nonapplicant elects to submit to the applicant rather than to FDA, the nonapplicant must submit each report to the applicant within 5 calendar days of initial receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nonapplicant must maintain a record including (A) a copy of each adverse drug experience report; (B) the date the report was received by the nonapplicant; (C) the date the report was submitted to the applicant; and (D) the name and address of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic reporting schedule (quarterly then annual)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must report each adverse drug experience not reported under paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section at quarterly intervals, for 3 years from the date of approval of the application, and then at annual intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each quarterly report must be submitted within 30 days of the close of the quarter (first quarter beginning on date of approval); each annual report within 60 days of the anniversary date of approval. FDA may extend or reestablish quarterly reporting or require different timing (e.g., after approval of a major supplement). Followup information may be submitted in the next periodic report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic report contents — descriptive information (narrative and analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each periodic report is required to contain: Descriptive information including (1) a narrative summary and analysis of the information in the report; (2) an analysis of the 15-day Alert reports submitted during the reporting interval (all 15-day Alert reports being appropriately referenced by the applicant's patient identification code, adverse reaction term(s), and date of submission to FDA); (3) a history of actions taken since the last report because of adverse drug experiences; and (4) an index consisting of a line listing of the applicant's patient identification code, and adverse reaction term(s) for all ICSRs submitted under paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of actions: labeling changes or studies initiated. The 15-day Alert report analysis must reference each alert by patient ID, reaction terms, and submission date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic report contents — ICSRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each periodic report must contain ICSRs for each adverse drug experience not reported under paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section (all serious, expected and nonserious adverse drug experiences). All such ICSRs must be submitted to FDA (either individually or in one or more batches) within the timeframe specified in paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section. ICSRs must only be submitted to FDA once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICSRs may be submitted individually or in batches; do not resubmit identical ICSRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to periodic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodic reporting, except for information regarding 15-day Alert reports, does not apply to adverse drug experience information obtained from postmarketing studies (whether or not conducted under an investigational new drug application), from reports in the scientific literature, and from foreign marketing experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such sources are excluded from periodic reporting requirements (but 15-day rules may still apply under other provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific literature 15-day reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A 15-day Alert report based on information in the scientific literature must be accompanied by a copy of the published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 15-day reporting requirements apply only to reports found in scientific and medical journals either as case reports or as the result of a formal clinical trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing studies and 15-day reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is not required to submit a 15-day Alert report under paragraph (c) of this section for an adverse drug experience obtained from a postmarketing study (whether or not conducted under an investigational new drug application) unless the applicant concludes that there is a reasonable possibility that the drug caused the adverse experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant judgment about reasonable possibility of causation determines 15-day reporting obligation for postmarketing studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICSR patient information required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: ICSRs include the following patient information: (i) Patient identification code; (ii) Patient age at the time of adverse drug experience, or date of birth; (iii) Patient gender; and (iv) Patient weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patient identity should be coded rather than providing names/addresses (see patient privacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: ICSR adverse drug experience fields
rubrics_metrics.description: ICSRs must include: (i) Outcome attributed to adverse drug experience; (ii) Date of adverse drug experience; (iii) Date of ICSR submission; (iv) Description of adverse drug experience (including a concise medical narrative); (v) Adverse drug experience term(s); (vi) Description of relevant tests, including dates and laboratory data; and (vii) Other relevant patient history, including preexisting medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise medical narrative and relevant test data should be included to characterize the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICSR suspect medical product fields
rubrics_metrics.description: ICSRs must include information about suspect medical product(s): (i) Name; (ii) Dose, frequency, and route of administration used; (iii) Therapy dates; (iv) Diagnosis for use (indication); (v) Whether the product is a prescription or nonprescription product; (vi) Whether the product is a combination product as defined in § 3.2(e); (vii) Whether adverse drug experience abated after drug use stopped or dose reduced; (viii) Whether adverse drug experience reappeared after reintroduction of drug; (ix) Lot number; (x) Expiration date; (xi) National Drug Code (NDC) number; and (xii) Concomitant medical products and therapy dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide dechallenge/rechallenge information and product identifiers where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICSR initial reporter information
rubrics_metrics.description: ICSRs must include initial reporter information: (i) Name, address, and telephone number; (ii) Whether the initial reporter is a health care professional; and (iii) Occupation, if a health care professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sufficient contact and reporter qualification information for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICSR applicant information fields
rubrics_metrics.description: ICSRs must include applicant information: (i) Applicant name and contact office address; (ii) Telephone number; (iii) Report source, such as spontaneous, literature, or study; (iv) Date the report was received by applicant; (v) Application number and type; (vi) Whether the ICSR is a 15-day "Alert report"; (vii) Whether the ICSR is an initial report or followup report; and (viii) Unique case identification number, which must be the same in the initial report and any subsequent followup report(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a consistent unique case ID across initial and followup reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic format for safety report submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety report submissions, including ICSRs, ICSR attachments, and the descriptive information in periodic reports, must be in an electronic format that FDA can process, review, and archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will issue guidance on how to provide the electronic submission (method of transmission, media, file formats, preparation and organization of files).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary waiver of electronic submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or nonapplicant may request, in writing, a temporary waiver of the electronic submission requirements in paragraph (g)(1) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers will be granted on a limited basis for good cause shown. FDA will issue guidance on requesting a waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple reports rule (avoid duplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant should not include in reports under this section any adverse drug experiences that occurred in clinical trials if they were previously submitted as part of the approved application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a report applies to a drug for which an applicant holds more than one approved application, submit to the application that was first approved. If a report refers to more than one drug marketed by an applicant, submit to the application for the drug listed first in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient privacy and coding
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant should not include in reports under this section the names and addresses of individual patients; instead, the applicant should assign a unique code for identification of the patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant should include the name of the reporter from whom the information was received even when the reporter is the patient. Names of patients, health care professionals, hospitals, and geographic identifiers in adverse drug experience reports are not releasable to the public under FDA public information regulations in part 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must maintain for a period of 10 years records of all adverse drug experiences known to the applicant, including raw data and any correspondence relating to adverse drug experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records should be sufficient to support reports and any FDA followup or audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to report or keep records
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to establish and maintain records and make reports required under this section, FDA may withdraw approval of the application and, thus, prohibit continued marketing of the drug product that is the subject of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance may lead to withdrawal of approval and prohibition of marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to each approved/abbreviated application
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant shall make the reports for each of its approved applications and abbreviated applications required under this section and section 505(k) of the act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting obligations apply per approved/abbreviated application.

rubrics_metrics.name: NDA—Field alert report timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall submit information about distributed drug products and articles to the FDA district office responsible for the facility involved within 3 working days of receipt by the applicant. The information may be provided by telephone or other rapid communication means, with prompt written followup. The report and its mailing cover should be plainly marked: 'NDA—Field Alert Report.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information required includes incidents causing the drug or its labeling to be mistaken for another article, bacteriological contamination, significant chemical/physical deterioration, or failure of distributed batches to meet specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall submit each year within 60 days of the anniversary date of U.S. approval of the application, two copies of the annual report to the FDA division responsible for reviewing the application, accompanied by Form FDA 2252.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual report must include the listed content items in the order specified (summary, distribution data, labeling, chemistry/manufacturing/controls changes, nonclinical studies, clinical data, postmarketing study status, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report — summary of significant new information
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual report must contain a brief summary of significant new information from the previous year that might affect the safety, effectiveness, or labeling of the drug product, and a brief description of actions the applicant has taken or intends to take as a result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary shall state whether pediatric labeling supplements have been submitted and whether new pediatric studies have been initiated. Where possible, provide an estimate of patient exposure, especially pediatrics, including dosage form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report — distribution data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report must include distribution data: NDC number, the total number of dosage units of each strength or potency distributed, and quantities distributed for domestic and foreign use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of financial or pricing data is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report — labeling and labeling changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual report must include currently used professional labeling, patient brochures or package inserts (if any), a representative sample of the package labels, and a summary of any changes in labeling made since the last report (or a statement if no changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of labeling required under § 201.100(d)(3) must be submitted in electronic format in a form FDA can process, review, and archive; submissions must comply with part 11 (with specified exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report — chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual report must include reports of experiences, investigations, studies, or tests involving chemical or physical properties or other properties of the drug only for new information that may affect FDA's previous conclusions about safety or effectiveness, and a full description of manufacturing and controls changes not requiring a supplemental application under § 314.70(b) and (c), listed by date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only new information that may affect prior FDA conclusions is required to be reported here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report — nonclinical and clinical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual report must include copies of unpublished reports and summaries of published reports of new toxicological findings in animal and in vitro studies; published clinical trials (or abstracts), summaries of completed unpublished clinical trials, and analysis of safety and efficacy data in the pediatric population and proposed labeling changes based on this information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review articles, promotional articles, press clippings, and papers without tabulations or summaries of original data should not be reported. A study is considered completed 1 year after it is concluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report — status reports of postmarketing study commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual report must include a status report of each postmarketing study of the drug product that is required by FDA or committed to in writing, including for pediatric studies; status reported annually until FDA notifies applicant that the commitment is fulfilled or no longer feasible/useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must include applicant name; product name; NDA/ANDA/supplement number; date of U.S. approval; date of study commitment; description sufficient to uniquely describe the study; schedule for completion and reporting (with original and revised schedules if revised); current status categorized as pending/ongoing/delayed/terminated/submitted; explanation of status including accrual numbers and reasons for revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of postmarketing study information — limits
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may publicly disclose information about postmarketing studies necessary to identify the applicant or establish study status, except it will not disclose trade secrets or information the disclosure of which would constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information described in § 20.61 (trade secrets) and § 20.63 (privacy protections) will not be publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional log of outstanding regulatory business
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report may, at the applicant's discretion, also contain a list of any open regulatory business with FDA concerning the drug product (e.g., unanswered correspondence lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is optional but intended to facilitate communications between FDA and the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisements and promotional labeling submission timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall submit specimens of mailing pieces and any other labeling or advertising devised for promotion of the drug product at the time of initial dissemination of the labeling and at the time of initial publication of the advertisement for a prescription drug product. Each submission must be accompanied by Form FDA-2253 and a copy of the product's current professional labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing pieces and labeling designed to contain samples must be complete except the sample may be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of permanent discontinuance or interruption in manufacturing (who & when)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant of a prescription drug product must notify FDA in writing of a permanent discontinuance of manufacture or an interruption in manufacturing likely to lead to a meaningful disruption in supply in the U.S. if (1) the drug is life supporting/life sustaining or intended for use in prevention/treatment of a debilitating disease/condition and (2) the drug is not a radiopharmaceutical drug product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications must be submitted electronically in a format FDA can process: at least 6 months prior to the date of the permanent discontinuance or interruption, or if 6 months notice not possible, as soon as practicable but no later than 5 business days after occurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification content for manufacturing discontinuance/interruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications must include: (1) name of the drug including the NDC; (2) name of applicant; (3) whether notification relates to permanent discontinuance or interruption; (4) description of reason for discontinuance or interruption; and (5) estimated duration of the interruption in manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may publish a drug shortages list (with specified elements) but may withhold information that would adversely affect public health or is protected by statutory exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug shortages public list and withholding criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will maintain a publicly available list of drugs determined to be in shortage, including names/NDCs, applicant names, reason category for shortage, and estimated duration. FDA may choose not to make certain information available if disclosure would adversely affect public health or if information is protected by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include GMP compliance, regulatory delay, shortages of ingredients, discontinuation, shipping delays, demand increase, or other. Protected information per 18 U.S.C. 1905 or 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) will not be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from sale reporting (within 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 calendar days of the withdrawal of an approved drug from sale, applicants who are manufacturers, repackers, or relabelers subject to part 207 must submit specified information (NDC, identity by established/proprietary name, application number, date expected no longer in commercial distribution, and FDA requests reason for withdrawal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants not subject to part 207 must submit similar information to the Drug Registration and Listing Office either electronically or in writing. Reporting under this provision constitutes compliance with § 207.57 to update drug listing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACNU failure — definitions and surveillance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACNU failure occurs upon specified events (failure associated with implementation or operationalization of a key element of an ACNU). The applicant must develop written procedures for the surveillance, receipt, evaluation, and reporting of ACNU failures to FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACNU = Additional Condition for Nonprescription Use. Procedures must govern how information about ACNU failures is captured and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACNU failure reporting content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Report of an ACNU failure must include required information (applicant contact, identifiable reporter, drug product name, description of ACNU failure) and additional information if available (strength, NDC, lot, initial reporter info, unique case id, ACNU failure terms, dates, location, concise narrative of circumstances, remedial action, corrective action). The applicant must submit the report as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days from the date when the applicant has acquired the minimum dataset for an ACNU failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional information about an earlier ACNU failure is later obtained, submit a follow-up report as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after obtaining the new information. Reports must be submitted electronically per § 314.80(g) unless a waiver is requested under § 314.90 or § 314.99. Maintain records for 10 years of ACNU failures and associated adverse drug experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement for multiple applications and patient identification (repeat of earlier rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For all reports required by this section, the applicant shall submit the information common to more than one application only to the application first approved, and shall not report separately on each application. Applicants should not include patient names/addresses; code names and retain codes to permit FDA to identify patients if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must maintain sufficient patient identification information to permit FDA to identify patients when needed (e.g., to investigate reports further or to verify reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver requests for regulatory requirements (§314.90)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may ask FDA to waive any requirement that applies under §§ 314.50 through 314.81. A waiver request under this section is required to be submitted with supporting documentation in an NDA, or in an amendment or supplement to an NDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may also ask FDA to waive any criteria of an adequate and well-controlled study described in § 314.126(b) under § 314.126(c); supporting documentation must accompany the waiver request.
